# macOS-only expected failures. See common.txt for the shared ones and
# README.md for what may go in here.

# Both of these assert an *upper* bound on how long SysSleep took, and a shared
# runner cannot honour one. Observed on macos-15 arm64:
#
#   SysSleep(1.333) took 1.360999 but should take between 1.333 and 1.359
#   SysSleep(0.016) took 0.14777  but should take between 0.016 and 0.042
#
# Sleeping longer than requested is permitted by every sleep API; the interval
# is a floor, not a ceiling. The second case overshoots a 26 ms tolerance by
# 106 ms, which is ordinary scheduler jitter on a heavily shared VM. Neither
# failure indicates anything about the interpreter.
#
# Listed for macOS only because that is where they have been seen. They did not
# fail on the Linux or Windows runs, and being timing dependent they are flaky
# rather than deterministic, so if they ever show up elsewhere they should be
# added there too rather than moved into common.txt on the assumption they will.
SYSSLEEP.testGroup/TEST_SLEEP_CONCURRENT
SYSSLEEP.testGroup/TEST_SLEEP_DURATION
